clue.text: Boy and girl eating cheese

indicators.note: the girl is eating, so the cheese goes inside her

parts.note: GAL is an informal word for a girl
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Two children are tucking into some cheese together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is a boy's name, so it is an example of a boy.

clue.text: Put in charge of factory, treated with full honours

definitions.meaning: a works is a factory, so someone handed it has been put in charge
the idiom for receiving the full treatment

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means received the full treatment, and literally means handed a factory.

clue.text: Right to get to bottom of writer's block

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom is the end, so the right comes after the writer

parts.note: J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan

explanation.surface: An author struggles with writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get to bottom of' places R below BARRIE in this down entry; the 's after 'writer' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is an obstacle that blocks the way, so a synonym of block.

clue.text: Observe fool speaking in unfriendly way

indicators.note: speaking signals that the words are heard spoken, not written

parts.note: to eye is to observe and silly is a fool, giving eye silly

explanation.surface: Watching someone foolish talk in a cold manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' means EYE SILLY said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something icily means in a cold, unfriendly manner.

clue.text: Disinclined to make effort, learner is given two forms of support

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
aid is one form of support
to back is another form of support

explanation.surface: A lazy student is propped up twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A laid-back person is relaxed and easygoing, unwilling to exert themselves.

clue.text: Fish passed round in special platter

indicators.note: something passed round is turned about, so the run of letters is read backwards
the fish is sitting in the words that follow, as a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A fish dish is handed round the table on a fancy serving plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run ECIALP inside 'special platter'; 'passed round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a common flatfish, an example of a fish.

clue.text: In short blue material woman appears more elegant

indicators.note: the woman is in the shortened word
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: blue films and books are pornography, porn
she stands for any woman

explanation.surface: A woman in a short blue dress looks smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue material' looks like a coloured fabric, but blue here means indecent; 'short' drops the last letter and 'In' wraps the result around the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Posher means smarter or more upmarket, so more elegant.

clue.text: Petrol additive I put in tank mistakenly and later conk out

indicators.note: a mistaken arrangement means the letters are jumbled
out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Putting a fuel additive in the tank the wrong way makes the engine die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' turns I TANK into ANTIK and 'out' turns CONK into NOCK; 'conk out' means break down.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-knock agents are added to petrol to stop engine knocking.

clue.text: Scoundrel promises to pay for rum

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A rogue signs IOUs for his drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in British English means odd or strange, which is curious.

clue.text: In academic institutions, French department's one with places to go round

parts.note: the Var is a department of south-east France

indicators.note: the places go round the one, holding it inside

parts.note: sites are places
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A region of France boasts a university with buildings dotted about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'department' is 'has', a link; the Var is a French administrative department.
explanation.definitionFit: Varsities is an informal British word for universities, which are academic institutions.

clue.text: Try not to win shot-put event?

definitions.meaning: to ... a game is to lose it deliberately
putting the shot is a kind of hurl, the question mark flagging the loose fit

explanation.definitionFit: To throw a contest means to lose on purpose, and a shot put is one kind of hurl.

clue.text: Entertained by a poet?

parts.note: a phrase for being treated to a lavish meal, whose two verbs rhyme like a poet's line

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means entertained with food and drink, and its rhyme suits a poet.

clue.text: One in 7 is like 13

indicators.note: the one is placed in the word for 7's answer

parts.note: the answer to 7-down means inquisitive, which is nosy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle linking three answers in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 13-across is HARD ROCK, music known for volume; 7-down means inquisitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard rock is loud music, so being like it means being loud.

clue.text: Problem with car making you burst into tears?

definitions.meaning: a car that stops working has suffered a mechanical failure
an emotional collapse into crying is also called this

explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown is both a vehicle failure and an emotional collapse with tears.

clue.text: Certainly not soft music

parts.note: music that is anything but gentle: a loud, heavy guitar style whose name begins with the opposite of soft

explanation.definitionFit: Hard rock is a loud, heavy style of rock music, the opposite of soft music.

clue.text: Foreigners assembled the GI's car badly

indicators.note: badly signals letters put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A soldier's car is put together poorly by foreign workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag was the German parliament, an assembly of people foreign to British solvers.

clue.text: Dope is surprisingly self-assured

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters turn out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone on drugs is oddly confident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the letters of DOPE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Poised describes someone composed and confident, a synonym of self-assured.

clue.text: Wife at length conserved energy for dancing

indicators.note: the at holds the length inside it, conserving it

parts.note: zing means energy or zest

explanation.surface: A wife takes care to save energy over a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Waltzing is a form of ballroom dancing.

clue.text: To make financial gain, prof must be so alert

definitions.text: To make financial gain, prof must be so alert

parts.words: To make financial gain, prof must be so alert
parts.note: a backwards charade: to turn prof into a word for financial gain it must go along with the letters IT, and the phrase so formed also means alert

explanation.surface: An academic who wants to earn money has to stay sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: PROF joined with IT spells PROFIT, the financial gain; the phrase so described also means alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable and quick to understand is called being alert in this informal sense.

clue.text: Our food put out for brightly-coloured bird

indicators.note: the food is spread out around the other word

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican food
taken as written

explanation.surface: We put out our food for a gaudy bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as setting food out for the bird, but it means the food is opened out around the other word. The bird is more often spelt turaco.
explanation.definitionFit: Turacos are brightly plumaged African birds.

clue.text: Evangelist's servant shot

parts.note: Mark is one of the four Evangelists, the Gospel writers
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A Gospel writer's servant was fired upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A good shot is someone skilled with a gun, a marksman.

clue.text: Low-rise, not properly finished and hot, like some buildings in Granada

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A squat building is unfinished and warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-rise' looks like one word; split it as LOW and RISE. 'not properly finished' drops the E from RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada's Alhambra is a famous example of Moorish architecture.

clue.text: Area covered by denture

parts.note: the part of the mouth that a set of false teeth sits against, the roof of the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: The palate is the roof of the mouth, covered by an upper denture plate.

clue.text: Boisterous players get plastered

parts.note: rough means boisterous, as in rough play
the cast are the players in a show

explanation.surface: Rowdy actors end up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To roughcast a wall is to coat it with coarse plaster, so roughcast means plastered.

clue.text: About to face largely riotous throng

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: rowdy means riotous

explanation.surface: An unruly mob is about to be confronted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last letter of ROWDY to leave ROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a throng of people, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lacking experience in class, make slow progress

indicators.note: the inexperience is placed in the class

parts.note: CL is the abbreviation for class
raw means inexperienced

explanation.surface: A new student in a lesson struggles along.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to move or advance very slowly.

clue.text: Has edited daily newspaper column

indicators.note: text that has been edited is altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British daily

explanation.surface: A paper's column has been cut by an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a pillar or column, especially the main part of one.

clue.text: In it, a goat becomes restless

definitions.text: In it, a goat becomes restless

indicators.note: the letters become restless and move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A goat gets jittery when inside something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes restless' rearranges IN IT A GOAT; the whole clue also pictures the restlessness the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a state of nervous restlessness, which the goat displays.

clue.text: Girl Guide leaders left in distress? Ring for the Scouts

indicators.note: the leaders and left are placed in the word for distress

parts.note: woe means distress

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of these words

explanation.surface: Guide leaders in trouble need help from the Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A woggle is the leather or plastic ring Scouts use to hold their neckerchiefs.

clue.text: Celebration held for knight

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
had means held, as in possessed

explanation.surface: A party is thrown in honour of a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad is the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
